risks.risk: Console may not actually work (faulty HDMI port, power supply issue, overheating, or disc drive problems).
risks.proof: A short video of powering on, reaching the PS4 home screen, and showing the controller working (plus audio/video output on a TV).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not guaranteed working (worst case: needs repair / may have display or boot issues).

risks.risk: Storage size and whether it has been wiped/ready for setup (HDD/SSD health).
risks.proof: Photo/screenshot of System Settings → Storage showing capacity, and System Settings → About showing software version.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown storage (worst case: lower capacity and/or not confirmed healthy).

risks.risk: Extra controller claim may be false or incomplete bundle.
risks.proof: Photo showing both controllers side-by-side (front and back), including any included accessories.

risks.risk: Region/UK origin claim may not matter, but could indicate different power/packaging or missing local warranty.
risks.proof: Photo of the console label/serial sticker and any box label/receipt details.

risks.risk: Accessories may be missing (HDMI cable, power cable, headset, etc.).
risks.proof: Lay out all items included and take a single photo showing each cable/accessory clearly.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming only what’s shown (console + controller + the visible USB cable), with other cables not guaranteed.

proof_requests: Power-on video showing PS4 boots to home screen and controller works (and TV display is visible).
Photo/screenshot of System Settings → Storage (capacity) and About (model/firmware).
Clear photo of the full bundle laid out (confirm whether there are 1 or 2 controllers).
Photo of the console serial/model label (sticker) and any included cables (HDMI + power cable if present).
response.reason: The photos identify a PS4 Slim and show a controller and cable, but the key value drivers—confirmed working status and whether an extra controller is included—are not proven from the single image.
